title: Air Ticket Fare Brands: Vouchers a Credit Reissue Fee Is Taken for
content:
How often the credit reissue fee falls due under Air Ticket Fare Brands follows the travel credit vouchers standing lapsed on the booking, and what falls due that many times is the tariff component. The desk reads the number of them from the travel credit vouchers issued on that booking, and reads from the terms of the fare brand that produced them whether that brand makes credits transferable.

Where two or more vouchers stand lapsed on the booking, the tariff component is taken once for each voucher standing lapsed on it. Where a single voucher stands lapsed on the booking and the fare brand that produced it makes credits transferable, the tariff component is taken once and increased by half again, that is at 1.5 times. Otherwise the tariff component is taken once.

| Vouchers standing lapsed on the booking | Credits under the fare brand that produced them | How often the tariff component is taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Two or more | Either | Once for each voucher standing lapsed on the booking |
| A single voucher | Transferable | Once, increased by half again, at 1.5 times |
| A single voucher | Non-transferable | Once |

The first clause draws no distinction by transferability: on a booking carrying three lapsed vouchers the tariff component is taken three times whether or not the fare brand makes credits transferable. Transferability tells only where a single voucher stands lapsed, and there it lifts the one taking of the tariff component by half again, at 1.5 times; where that brand makes credits non-transferable the single taking of the tariff component stands as it is.
